findings.title: Missing repair file association is mislabeled as historical/unbound evidence
findings.detail: The current checked reference submission and ledger identity are both bound. Its one finding has no repair.before/after, so the item is retained in unbound_items. The UI then calls appendItem(..., false), renders all 13 locatable references as historical/unbound (including status=ok), and disables their navigation. This is not item loss or an untrusted current document; it is missing repair-file association.
findings.recommendation: Separate file association from document/reference identity. Keep the item in an unassociated group; preserve current authenticated raw-reference navigation. Do not invent repair endpoints or attach it to root.

findings.title: Recorded-transition-only graph omits checked explicit model edges
findings.detail: C4 has one explicit mechanically true write edge in its submitted YAML; Member has two. All are omitted by the current graph's recorded_transitions scope. This is current contract behavior, not lost query history. Pure search entries and the self-loop are correctly not promoted to read/write lines.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate a separate explicit-declaration source with ledger/raw-action validation; retain all original trajectory steps unchanged.

limitations: These tests authenticate rendering, document provenance and bounded relation checks, not model causal accuracy or complete repair discovery.
Current runs do not navigate the old Member v16→agent v5/v33 pairs; a separate frozen-source current-ledger regression checks those pairs without rebinding any old run.
Neither actual graph has a ledger stub, so true stub expansion is not claimed. Findings/reason expansion, candidate toggles, real atom drawer completion and resize are covered.
C4 0/0 and Member 38/38 are coverage-accounting results, not all-repair semantic verification; Member retains 19 deferred/unconfirmed records.
